newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Random violence, clashes hit luckless Albania.
newsitem.headline: Random violence, clashes hit luckless Albania.

text.p: Protests, clashes and random violence hit Albania again on Thursday amid fears that more get-rich-quick investment schemes could collapse and plunge the Balkan country further into crisis.
Western governments expressed concern, warning nationals to be careful. They discussed ways to help Europe's poorest state to head off a possible new wave of mass immigration.
Italy advised its nationals to consider restricting travel within and to Albania over the next few days, following recent bloody riots and anti-government protests.
France, voicing "extreme concern", said the European Union was discussing ways of helping end the crisis through dialogue between the right-wing government and the opposition.
The worst clash was in the town of Fier, south of Tirana, where a group of civilians armed with wooden clubs and iron bars attacked several thousand anti-government protesters.

For a month, Albanians have demonstrated to demand that the right-wing government of President Sali Berisha reimburse them for millions of dollars which were lost when several dubious high interest investment schemes collapsed.
Witnesses in Fier, 120 km ( 80 miles) south of Tirana, said at least six people were injured. Three people went to hospital, including a 50-year-old man who risks losing his eye.
"We came out with flowers and they attacked us," members of the crowd shouted. Police at a nearby station stood by and did not intervene, the witnesses said.
Police cordoned off Tirana's Skanderbeg Square on Thursday to prevent anti-government demonstrations but protesters took to the streets for a ninth day in Vlore, further south of Fier.
Several thousand demonstrators chanted "Give us our money" and "Resign, resign", blaming the government for letting the schemes flourish for the past five years.
The Vlore demonstrators burned copies of a pro-government newspaper, overturned vegetable and fruit stands at the local market and shout "Government. Thief".
Vlore has been hit by a wave of violence since police were stoned, stripped and forced to leave the town earlier this week in clashes which left three people dead.
A policeman was shot dead on Wednesday, another officer's house was attacked and a teenage girl was abducted from her home, apparently to be sold to a prostitution ring, police said.

In Tirana, several men seized the car of the opposition Socialist Party Secretary General, Rexhep Mejdani, on Thursday, drove it to a village and dumped it off a cliff. Mejdani was not in the car when it was seized in central Tirana.
Europe's poorhouse, emerging from 40 years of isolation and Stalinist rule in 1990, Albania has been rocked by a month of protests after several investment schemes collapsed.

Hundreds of thousands of Albanians from all walks of life lost their life savings in the popular "pyramid" schemes, which often used money from new investors to cover high yield returns for earlier investors.

Diplomats and officials have said much of the money pumped into the schemes came from illegal trade in refugees and drugs as well as illegal Albanian workers in EU countries, who sent their earnings home to relatives.

But doctors, lawyers, government officials and average Albanians also poured money into the schemes, thought to have total investments of some $2 billion -- a sum equal roughly to Albania's annual gross domestic product.

A failed Vlore scheme was estimated to have had investments of $500 million. The government froze the assets of two other schemes totalling $300 million and is paying out a percentage of that to luckless investors.
In a newspaper interview published on Thursday, Prime Minister Alexander Meksi said that the government could do no more than hand out the money which it had frozen.

Asked if the government would cover other losses, he said: "No. We are distributing the money we have managed to freeze in the banks. That's all we can do. It would be nonsense for us to try to take the place of the failed schemes."
